sections.h2: Which office sends the Boca Raton property tax bill?
sections.html:
One bill arrives from the Palm Beach County Tax Collector, and the Property Appraiser sets the value. The city itself levies only a slice.

The city's August 2026 Property Taxes Explained brochure says a Boca Raton bill carries eight taxing authorities and that only 21.67 percent of the tax goes to the city. The Tax Collector's page says it mails more than 600,000 bills by November 1 to the address on file with the Property Appraiser, and that taxes are payable November 1 through March 31.

  • Value, exemptions and mailing address: Palm Beach County Property Appraiser, (561) 355-2866.
  • Bills, delinquent tax, installment plan, deferral, tax certificates: Palm Beach County Tax Collector, delinquent line (561) 355-2264.
  • City levy and fire assessment: City of Boca Raton, 201 West Palmetto Park Road.

sections.h2: Which taxing authorities appear on a Boca Raton bill?
sections.html:
The city brochure lists eight: the Palm Beach County School Board, Palm Beach County operating and debt, Boca Raton operating and debt, the Health Care District, the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District, the Children's Services Council, the South Florida Water Management District and the Florida Inland Navigational District.

The brochure prints a total millage of 16.9090 for its sample, labeled with the 2026-27 column and published during the proposed-rate stage. Confirm the adopted rate for your own parcel on the Property Appraiser's tax roll tools, since taxing districts inside the city differ by location.

sections.h2: What has the Boca Raton city rate done over time?
sections.html:
The city's rate history chart shows the operating rate near 3.45 mills in 2018 and 3.6476 mills for both 2026 and 2027, while a separate debt service rate fell from 0.2245 to 0.0163 over the same span.

Combined, the city's total millage moved only between 3.6788 and 3.6639 across the ten years charted. The brochure's 2027 column is the city's proposed figure, so it reads as a plan, not a final bill. The city's own slice has stayed steady, so bigger swings come from the school board and county lines.

The brochure also compares Boca Raton's fire assessment, which it prints at $170.00, with other South Florida cities, and says unincorporated Palm Beach County pays a fire MSTU based on assessed value instead. Fire assessments are non-ad valorem, so they sit on the bill beside the millage.

sections.h2: What does the Boca Raton levy pay for?
sections.html:
The city brochure puts its own operating budget at $723,811,900, with 1,951 full time equivalent employees, 224 police officers and 269 firefighters working from 8 fire stations.

It reports 47,161 police calls and 18,872 fire and rescue calls a year, 49 parks covering 1,072.03 acres of parks and trails, a AAA bond rating and a land area of 31.59 square miles. The cost to operate police and fire is printed at $172.3 million against proposed property taxes of $150.2 million.

A buyer asking why a Boca Raton bill looks the way it does can be pointed to the brochure, which also shows each authority's share of the $693,362,086 residents pay in total annually. The School Board takes 37.18 percent and Palm Beach County operating and debt takes 26.74 percent.

sections.h2: When are Boca Raton property taxes due?
sections.html:
Pay between November and March. Delinquency begins in April, and March brings no discount.

The Palm Beach County Tax Collector prints the early payment ladder: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January, 1 percent in February, no discount in March and delinquency in April. Gross tax is due March 31. The Tax Collector adds that a deadline landing on a weekend or holiday slides forward to the following business day.

Once delinquent, the tax cannot be paid online, and the postmark is no longer proof of payment. Payments must arrive by the last working day of the month to count for that month. Delinquent balances can be confirmed through the Tax Collector's delinquent line.

sections.h2: How do exemptions and caps work for Boca Raton homes?
sections.html:
Homestead applications go to the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser. The deadline is March 1, and the house must be your permanent home on January 1.

The city brochure's sample shows the structure: a $50,000 homestead exemption against most levies and $25,000 against school district tax, matching the state rule that the second $25,000 does not apply to school taxes. The brochure's footnote says Amendment 1 gave a double homestead exemption for all levies except school.

  • Save Our Homes restrains yearly assessed value growth to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower. Florida's chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • Portability can carry the benefit to a new homestead within three years.
  • A sale means a new owner is assessed at full just value the following January.
  • Seniors, disabled veterans and deployed servicemembers have separate exemptions through state law and local ordinance.

sections.h2: What do Boca Raton's numbers mean for a seller?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 101,582 residents in July 2025 in a city of about 29 square miles of land, with owners living in 65.7 percent of homes and a $722,700 median value in the 2020 to 2024 data.

Median gross rent is $2,508 and median household income is $106,273. Residents 65 and over make up 24.6 percent of the population, so plenty of sellers are retirees downsizing or heirs settling an estate. The city says it has 49,050 dwelling units and an assessed value of $42.7 billion.

At those values, tax effects at closing are large. Florida's deed stamp tax, 70 cents per $100 of price outside Miami-Dade, falls on every party to the deed. The closing statement should divide the year's tax and any fire assessment.

sections.h2: What if a Boca Raton owner falls behind on tax?
sections.html:
Contact the Tax Collector before the April delinquency date, since delinquent tax cannot be paid through the online portal and a payment mailed late is judged by its arrival date, not the postmark. Keep the bill number from the Property Control Number box on the notice handy when you call. The Tax Collector lists an installment plan and a homestead tax deferral among its resources.

State rules put deferral applications at March 31 with Form DR-570, and installment applications at May 1 of the assessment year. Tax certificates are sold by June 1, a holder can seek a tax deed after two years, and on homestead property the opening deed bid includes half the assessed value.

A house with a certificate can still be sold, and the payoff is made from proceeds at closing. Request a written payoff from the Tax Collector, because delinquent balances change as months pass.

faqs.q: Does the City of Boca Raton send its own tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The Palm Beach County Tax Collector sends one bill that includes the city and seven other taxing authorities, per the city's brochure.

faqs.q: What is the Boca Raton millage rate?
faqs.a: It depends on the location. The city's brochure prints 3.6639 mills for the city operating and debt levy and a sample total of 16.9090, labeled as the 2026-27 proposed figure. Check your parcel's adopted rate with the Property Appraiser.

faqs.q: When do Boca Raton property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Gross tax is due March 31, and delinquent tax cannot be paid online.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about a Boca Raton exemption?
faqs.a: The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser, at (561) 355-2866. Applications are due on March 1.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my Save Our Homes cap?
faqs.a: No. A change of ownership resets assessed value to just value the following January 1, with limited exceptions such as certain spousal transfers.
